newsitem.title: USA: NYC Water Authority gets positive outlook from S&P.
newsitem.headline: NYC Water Authority gets positive outlook from S&P.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp Monday said it issued a positive rating outlook for the New York City Water Finance Authority, citing several factors, including less of a risk that it would have to build a costly plant.
Seth Lehman, an analyst with the rating agency, explained the outlook, which reflects the agency's view for the next one to three years, sets the Authority up for a possible upgrade.

"We're looking for the trend to continue. If they show us the same signals we see today, we'd probably look to upgrade them," Lehman said, but cautioned no action was likely for at least a year, as reassessments usually are conducted each year.

Standard and Poor's Corp at present gives the Authority's bonds an A-minus rating, while debt sold through the state Environmental Facilities Corp is rated a single-A, as it has additional reserves. Moody's Investors Service on Friday also gave the Water Authority a positive outlook.

The agency is in the midst of a retail presale period for about $365 million of bonds. On Friday, the first day of the two-day period, only $4 million of bonds were ordered by individual investors, a disappointing result that was due to the two-point drop in Treasury bonds prices, which stumbled badly after economic reports on payrolls and the manufacturing sector showed surprising strength.

There was speculation on Monday morning that the Authority would issue a new retail scale by as early as 0930 EDT, which would offer investors higher yields. A New York City water official was not immediately available to comment.

In addition to the possibility that last spring's agreement with enviromental regulators has removed -- at least for now -- the threat that the Authority might have to build an approximately $4 billion water filtration plant, Lehman noted rate increases were projected to moderate, and added the agency has a record of being able to raise prices when necessary.
